name: the-window-opens-itself-again
why: The whole slice: 'Notify, then you choose' (Mac). The enhanced skin must not slam a full-screen window over a player mid-swing.

name: the-classic-skin-loses-its-sheet
new:
say?.('You have gained a level!');
    return false;
why: DFU posts dfuiOpenCharacterSheetWindow (RaiseSkills :1414) and the classic lane is byte-for-byte what it was before this slice.

name: the-reminder-is-remembered-instead-of-read
old: if (!owed) continue;                         // spent, by any road - the reminder is state, not memory
why: A level spent by the window, the font-less escape, a headless roll or a load leaves a line on screen telling the player to spend it again.

name: a-level-owed-but-never-announced-says-nothing
why: A save loaded with the flag set, or a level earned while the surface was not mounted: the strip is the only place that says a level is waiting.

name: the-standing-reminder-still-calls-itself-news
old: out.push({ ...r, standing, title: standing ? AWAITS_TITLE : r.title });

name: the-level-row-moves-under-the-player
old: return out.sort((a, b) => (Number(a.kind === NOTICE_LEVEL) - Number(b.kind === NOTICE_LEVEL)) || (b.seq - a.seq));
why: raiseSkills raises the skills and THEN levels the player, so a plain newest-first sort puts the one row that asks for something in a different place every time.

name: the-cap-eats-the-level
why: A rest raises a handful of skills in one pass; the row a player is looking for must not be the one pushed off the strip.

name: the-window-replays-the-fanfare-the-strip-played
why: One event, one sound: the strip plays it where the level was earned and the window may not open for ten minutes.

name: the-hidden-HUD-keeps-its-strip
why: AUDIT 64 F37: a persistent DOM overlay stays painted unless told otherwise.

name: the-strip-names-a-key-nobody-bound
why: FIX-F's bug and MAC-C's, one layer down: a rebound key the screen still names by its default.

name: the-key-chip-rides-every-row
old:
if (r.kind === NOTICE_LEVEL && codeForAction(bindings(), 'CharacterSheet') != null) {
    const k = doc.createElement('span');
why: A skill line with a key on it reads as an instruction.

name: the-inverse-lookup-answers-the-secondary-first
why: EQUIVALENT at the shipped bindings, where no action carries a secondary code - and the ORDER is still the law (actionForCode resolves primary first, so the key this names must be the key that answers). Recorded rather than chased: a pin that needed a second binding to exist would be pinning the fixture, not the port.

name: a-host-stops-announcing
new:
hudText.add('You have gained a level!');
    api.toggleCharSheet();
why: THE FOUR HOSTS RULE: the answer to 'does the window open itself' is written once, or it is written four times and drifts.

name: the-unspent-level-shouts-once-per-rest
why: AUDIT LV2 F2. checkForLevelUp stays TRUE while `level` is behind the calculated one, so every later raise pass reaches this arm: without the guard an unspent level replayed the fanfare and knocked its own standing reminder back into news, once per rest, until it was spent.

name: a-genuinely-new-level-goes-unannounced
why: AUDIT LV2 F2, the other way round, and EQUIVALENT at every reachable state - recorded rather than chased. `announcedLevel` is non-null only while a level is announced AND owed, and while a level is owed `checkForLevelUp` pins `pendingLevel` at `level + 1` (systems/advancement.js:207) because `level` does not advance until the points are spent - so the level asked about IS the level announced, and the two guards cannot disagree. The guard is still written as the QUESTION (`fanfareOwed`, the same one ui/charSheetDoor.js asks) rather than as the latch: `announcedLevel != null` would be coupling to an invariant nothing states, and a pin that made the two disagree would have to build a `pendingLevel` no road in the port produces - pinning the fixture, not the port.

name: the-strip-goes-back-on-the-body
why: AUDIT LV2 F4. `.hud-bottom` grows upward with its content and with --hud-scale; a body-level strip at a fixed offset sat 19px into the vitals at scale 1 on a phone and 154px into them at scale 2.

name: the-strip-hangs-under-the-vitals-instead-of-over-them
why: AUDIT LV2 F4. Appended, the strip becomes the column's LAST row - under the needs strip and hard against the foot of the screen, which is the overlap it was moved to avoid.

name: the-strip-is-taken-home-only-once
why: AUDIT LV2 F4. drawHud builds the HUD host on the call AFTER this one, so a strip raised on the first frame of a session lands on the body and must be moved home on the next.

name: the-mastery-rows-are-read-on-both-lanes-again
why: AUDIT LV2 F3. An argument is not a thunk: passed by value, TEXT.RSC record 4020 came off disk on the enhanced lane too and was dropped, under a module whose header promises no game data is read to announce a mastery.

name: the-row-names-a-key-called-None
why: AUDIT LV2 F5. buttonText(null) is KeyCode.None's own string, so a player who cleared the sheet binding was told to press NONE.

name: the-pool-is-re-rolled-on-every-open-again
new:
entity.pendingBonusPool = LEVELUP_BONUS_POOL_MIN + Math.floor(rolls() * (LEVELUP_BONUS_POOL_MAX + 1 - LEVELUP_BONUS_POOL_MIN));
  return entity.pendingBonusPool;
why: AUDIT LV2, reopened (Mac: 'Yes fucking fix it'). The draw is the LEVEL'S, not the window's: without the memo, closing the enhanced level-up window and pressing the sheet key again rolls a new 4..6, so a player escapes and re-opens until it says 6.

name: the-spent-level-keeps-its-pool
old:
entity.pendingLevel = null;
  entity.pendingBonusPool = null;   // the level is spent, so its pool is not pending either
why: The other half: a pool that outlives its level hands the NEXT level the number the last one rolled, so a lucky 6 is a 6 forever.

name: the-oghma-arm-keeps-the-pool-it-did-not-spend
old:
entity.pendingLevel = null;
    entity.pendingBonusPool = null;   // the book's thirty is fixed, but a level owed UNDER it was pending too
why: The Infinium's thirty is fixed and is not this draw, but the level it eats WAS pending - and AUDIT 39's finding is that this arm is the one that clears the shared flag. Its pool goes with it.

name: the-window-rolls-its-own-pool-again
new: this.pool = this.oghma ? OGHMA_BONUS_POOL : LEVELUP_BONUS_POOL_MIN + Math.floor(rolls() * (LEVELUP_BONUS_POOL_MAX + 1 - LEVELUP_BONUS_POOL_MIN));
why: One home for the draw. A screen that rolls its own is the exploit back, whatever the entity remembers.

name: the-pool-does-not-ride-the-save
why: A pool that does not survive the save is re-rolled by a save and a load - the same exploit through a slower door.
